uncited: - **Inputs:** Measured images $\{i_{c,\mu}^{measured}\}$ for views $c=1 \dots N_{views}$ and channels $\mu \in \{R, G, B\}$; camera parameters; physical constants ($\sigma_{\mu}^{aerosol}, \beta_{\mu}^{air}$); regularization weight $\eta$; step size $\Delta$; number of gradient steps per surrogate update $NGD$.
- $j_{all}^{(q)}$: Field of radiance values $\{j_{c,\mu}^{(q)}\}$ computed via Forward Monte Carlo (FMC) at iteration $q$.
- **Sun Masking:** Pixels around the Sun are masked ($M_c$) because Monte Carlo estimates have high variance due to forward scattering phase function sampling.
- **Ill-conditioning:** Voxels near cameras have unstable $\beta$ estimates because they affect more pixels, leading to higher gradient magnitudes.
- **Time Complexity:** Direct Jacobian computation requires $O(N_{voxels})$ FMC renderings per iteration, which is computationally expensive.
- **Memory Complexity:** Requires storing the radiance field $j_{all}$ and the extinction field $\beta$.
